findings.F1: The book fails only on Calmar (0.748 against 0.75); its pooled daily equity falls 46.2% at its deepest. The deepest falls inside windows are w9 (-40.5%), w13 (-36.2%), w14 (-32.9%), w2 (-32.3%) and w3 (-32.2%). In each of these the coins themselves fell 44% to 68%.
findings.F2: The book's falls come from crash days that hit every coin at once. On the book's 30 worst days its daily return averaged -13.8%, against -9.8% for the coins' mean. On those days 98.9% of the coin-days the book held lost money.
findings.F3: The gain sits in the large positions. Bars with a forecast of 16 or more (n=1280, one-bar horizon, so the cases are independent) earn 0.62% above the coin's all-window mean (t 3.80), with a hit rate of 0.608. The small positions with a forecast in (0,5] (n=6068) earn only 0.02% above the coin's mean (t 0.40), so they keep the book exposed to the crash days with no edge.
findings.F4: Where the drop happens relative to the 50-day average decides whether it pays:
findings.F5: The prior five days tell the same story. After a five-day fall of more than 10%, active bars earn 0.92% above the coin's mean (t 3.66, n=889). After a shallow five-day fall of 0% to 3%, they earn -0.22% (t -2.29, n=1324).

ideas.idea: A coin rebounds the next day after a down day when that day comes on top of a deep fall already under way, its close more than about a fifth below its 50-day average or more than a tenth below its close of five days earlier. When the fall is only moderate, the next day keeps drifting lower.
ideas.consequence: Take the rebound long only after a drop that deepens an already large decline, and refuse it during moderate declines, where the book takes losses on the crash days that set its drawdown.
ideas.name: rebound needs capitulation depth

ideas.idea: A coin's next-day rebound after a down day appears when its recent daily moves are larger than its usual size, and is stronger the more volatile the recent days are. In calm periods a down day is followed by a slightly weaker than average next day.
ideas.consequence: Hold the rebound long only when the coin's trailing volatility is above its norm, and stay flat after small drops in calm periods, which carry exposure without gain.
ideas.name: rebound lives in high volatility
